demonstrated_gap: New to the catalog. It addresses two recorded open gaps of the winner. (a) ai-memory captures sanitized assistant excerpts capped at 2,000 bytes, and Claude prompt capture is opted out. deja instead indexes the complete native transcripts that Claude Code and Codex already write, with no capture step and no model, and redacts credentials at index time. (b) ai-memory deletion covered only current search results. `deja forget` writes tombstones so a rebuilt index cannot restore forgotten sessions. It also offers `deja handoff --to codex`. Vendor measurements on the same 470-question cleaned LongMemEval-S set, with no LLM and no embeddings: hit@5 97.4% and evidence-recall@5 91.5%; capture costs zero model tokens. Risks: lexical ranking (preference slice 43.3% hit@1); a pooled 19,195-session haystack drops to 19% hit@1; a single maintainer; OpenSSF Code-Review 0/10; no npm provenance; 858 commits in 30 days. Source transcripts stay unredacted, and `deja secrets --scrub` rewrites native transcripts, so it must stay disabled in any trial.
comparison_that_would_overturn: Add deja (v0.21.2 binary verified by checksum) as an arm in the preregistered harness: recall_all@5 on the 470 manifest with a fresh store per question, plus a pooled-store run, against C3/C4 and D2. Then run an isolated lifecycle probe on a synthetic transcript corpus: tombstone persistence across reindex, restore from backup, a redaction audit with planted credentials, and complete usage. It is overturned if recall_all@5 does not beat C4 by at least +5 pp, if pooled recall falls below ai-memory's, or if tombstones or redaction fail.
